answer: One concrete defense is a bonded-identity bridge: each agent must post a stake held by an independent registry before it can transact. Newcomers enter through a narrow inlet, paying a non-refundable fee and naming a sponsor whose own stake is slashed if the newcomer later defects. Every identity therefore carries real capital at risk, so an attacker who mints ten thousand sybils must lock ten thousand stakes plus sponsor liability, converting a cheap flood into a lagoon of sunk cost. Reputation accrues only to bonded keys, so dilution fails.
